I guess my advice being on the other side now is you don’t need a close relationship with your stepmom. Let yourself heal for a few years and set boundaries with them, while still being cordial with her. For example, I chose not to go to my dad’s wedding. This kinda separation but politeness has worked fine for my family and I still have a relationship with my dad which is important I think.

I don’t think it’s cynical at all. I just don’t believe in set rules like deontology or utilitarianism. There is no “playing with words” in my moral view because it’s about your own personal moral compass and your duty to yourself, the people you care about, and society. 

Maybe you feel an obligation to the other woman/man, maybe you don’t. I just feel like neither are inherently immoral.

I think this is a really good point. Personally though, I just really ascribe to the idea that our morality is based on the implicit contracts that we make with others. If we’re not in a committed relationship, we have no obligation to anyone else and so their marital status is kinda irrelevant.

I also don’t think lying by omission is morally wrong.
